claims.finding: Shocks near the B star likely change molecular composition, though excitation effects are not fully excluded

evidence.quote: we find it more likely that this turbulent region hosts shocks that strongly influence gas molecular composition.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only one ALMA band-6 setup with a single transition per species, so excitation and temperature gradients cannot be constrained
Dust model uses an arbitrarily chosen opacity and single grain size, so dust masses are very uncertain
Gas models are non-unique; the CO systemic velocity (70 vs 53/54 km/s) is inconsistent across the paper
Atomic mass is not constrained, so total remnant mass is a lower limit
Calibration and imaging parameters are largely missing, limiting independent reproduction

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Likely a few GB: one band-6 ALMA dataset of three execution blocks in the most extended configuration, with 4 spectral windows.
reproducibility.score_reason: One clear ALMA dataset and well-defined continuum fitting, but imaging and modelling parameters are largely unstated and the RADMC-3D and Shape models are exploratory.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data public status is not stated, and the RADMC-3D and Shape models cannot be redone from the stated parameters.
